commit.message:
Allow copying symbolic links when Developer Mode is enabled on Windows

Prior to this patch, invoking `File.copy()` for copying symbolic links
without following links (i.e. with the flag LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS`)
causes an `AccessDeniedException` exception when the code is run without
elevated privileges when Developer Mode is enabled.  This is because the
`File.copy()` call ultimately invokes the `CopyFileEx()` Win32 API
function, which requires elevated privileges to copy symbolic links.

Instead of copying symbolic links using `CopyFileEx()`, we can instead
recreate the destination symbolic link using the `CreateSymbolicLink()`
Win32 API function, which permits creating symbolic links even without
elevated privileges when `SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE`
is among the flags passed to the function.  This enables the CopyAndMove
test to pass on Windows when Developer Mode is enabled.

The key change in this patch is that `WindowsFileCopy.copy()` now
recognizes when the source file is a symbolic link and if the copy
operation is on the symbolic link itself (rather than the target of the
symbolic link), then it calls `WindowsLinkSupport.createSymbolLink()` to
create a new symbolic link to the target of the original symbolic link.

Validated this patch by running test/jdk tier1, tier2, and tier3 tests
on a FastDebug build.
